To mark Donald Trump's 80th birthday, here are 80 things you should know about
the sitting president of the United States (who will leave office in January
2029 as the oldest president in the history of the country).

  1. **His father was a real estate mogul**

     * Donald Trump's father, Fred Trump, was a prominent real estate developer who [built](https://www.nytimes.com/1999/06/26/nyregion/fred-c-trump-postwar-master-builder-of-housing-for-middle-class-dies-at-93.html) more than 27,000 apartments and row houses across New York City.

  2. **His mother was an immigrant**

     * Mary Anne Trump [immigrated](https://www.newyorker.com/news/news-desk/donald-trumps-immigrant-mother) to the U.S. from Scotland in 1930, having learned English as a [second language](https://www.politico.com/magazine/story/2017/11/03/mary-macleod-trump-donald-trump-mother-biography-mom-immigrant-scotland-215779/).

  3. **He grew up in a mansion**

     * Donald Trump grew up in a 23-room brick [mansion](https://www.nytimes.com/2017/08/21/nyregion/trump-childhood-home-queens.html) in the affluent neighborhood of Jamaica Estates, Queens. 

  4. **He became a millionaire at just eight years old**

     * According to a _New York Times_ [investigation](https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2018/10/02/us/politics/donald-trump-tax-schemes-fred-trump.html), by the age of three, Donald Trump earned today's equivalent of more than $200,000 a year, making him a millionaire by the age of eight.

  5. **He was seen as the favorite son**

     * Donald Trump was seen as the [favorite](https://www.nytimes.com/2016/01/03/us/politics/for-donald-trump-lessons-from-a-brothers-suffering.html) of the three Trump boys, taking over his eldest brother's position as the apparent heir to the Trump real estate empire. 

  6. **He does not drink alcohol**

     * Speaking of Trump's eldest brother, Freddy [developed alcoholism](https://www.nytimes.com/2016/01/03/us/politics/for-donald-trump-lessons-from-a-brothers-suffering.html) in the 1960s and died of a heart attack at the age of 42. Donald Trump [cites this](https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-38651623) as the reason he doesn't drink.

  7. **His late sister was a Clinton-appointed judge**

     * Maryanne Trump Barry was [appointed](https://www.businessinsider.com/maryanne-trump-barry-bio-judge-president-trump-sister-2018-8) by President Bill Clinton to the U.S. Court of Appeals in 1999, serving in the role for 16 years before retiring amid an [investigation](https://www.nytimes.com/2019/04/10/us/maryanne-trump-barry-misconduct-inquiry.html) into whether she had committed tax fraud. Guess it runs in the family.

  8. **He was sent to military school**

     * Donald Trump was sent to [the New York Military Academy](https://www.pbs.org/wgbh/frontline/article/trump-the-bully-how-childhood-military-school-shaped-the-future-president/) at the age of 13, where he was [described](https://www.washingtonpost.com/lifestyle/style/young-donald-trump-military-school/2016/06/22/f0b3b164-317c-11e6-8758-d58e76e11b12_story.html) by many of his classmates as a "bully." Are we surprised?

  9. **Yet … he dodged the Vietnam War draft**

     * Despite attending military school, Trump did not, in fact, go on to serve in the military during the Vietnam War. He avoided the draft [five times](https://www.businessinsider.com/donald-trump-avoided-the-military-draft-which-was-common-at-the-time-vietnam-war-2018-12): the first four were to complete his college degree, and the fifth time, he was diagnosed with [bone spurs](https://www.nytimes.com/2018/12/26/us/politics/trump-vietnam-draft-exemption.html) that would disqualify him from service.

  10. **He graduated from the University of Pennsylvania 's Wharton School of Business**

     * Trump has repeatedly claimed he graduated at the top of his class in 1968, yet, Wharton's published academic honors and deans lists for that year [do not mention his name](https://www.thedp.com/article/2017/02/trump-academics-at-wharton). Awkward.

  11. **He 's a nepo baby**

     * After graduating from the University of Pennsylvania, Trump immediately began working for his father. He became [president](https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-35318432) of the Trump Organization a whopping three years later.

  12. **He and his father were sued for discrimination**

     * The Justice Department [sued](https://apnews.com/events-united-states-presidential-election-6349efef6986435b95411dc2e8f8f2c4) the Trumps in 1973 for refusing to rent apartments in predominantly white buildings to Black tenants.

  13. **But he did not have to admit to using discriminatory practices**

     * The case ended in a [settlement](https://apnews.com/events-united-states-presidential-election-6349efef6986435b95411dc2e8f8f2c4) that did not require the Trumps to explicitly acknowledge that they used discriminatory practices. However, the government's description of the settlement says they "[failed and neglected](https://clearinghouse-umich-production.s3.amazonaws.com/media/doc/83283.pdf)" to comply with the Fair Housing Act.

  14. **Roy Cohn was one of his closest friends and mentors**

     * Roy Cohn, who once worked for Sen. Joseph McCarthy as a ["Red Scare" prosecutor](https://www.history.com/articles/roy-cohn-mccarthyism-rosenberg-trial-donald-trump), became one of Trump's closest allies, and the two [reportedly](https://www.nytimes.com/2016/06/21/us/politics/donald-trump-roy-cohn.html?_r=0) spoke on the phone up to five times per day.
